summary: Added a Flow Engine to myiotsan: a Node-RED-style visual, executable data-flow canvas for wiring telemetry into computed values, alerts, and (guarded) actuation, shipped across three phases (P1 engine, P2 canvas, P3 templates + derived metric). A flow is a new entity (`IotFlow`, `apps/myiotsan/entities/iot_flow.go`) storing a node/wire graph as one JSON document, authored on a new admin-only frontend page (`apps/myiotsan/views/react-webpack/src/views/components/flows.js`): a flow list plus an SVG drag-and-drop canvas (palette, wiring, per-node config panel, zoom), reachable from a new "Flows" entry under the Automation nav group and new i18n keys (`flows.*`) in all four locales. The node palette (`apps/myiotsan/services/flows.go`) covers an input (`device_telemetry`, emits on a new reading), transforms (`scale`, and `function`/`expression`/`switch` -- arbitrary JavaScript), logic (`threshold`, `deadband`), and outputs (`debug` for the live inspector, `notify` to raise an alert, `command` to actuate, and `derived_metric` (P3) to persist a computed value as a new telemetry series). `parseGraph` validates every graph at save and again at compile: closed node-type set, no dangling wires, no cycles, a 200-node sanity ceiling. `services.FlowRuntime` (new `apps/myiotsan/services/flow_runtime.go`) compiles a graph and runs it on its own worker goroutine, tapping the SAME decoded-sample stream `RuleService.OnReading` does (new `Ingest.SetFlows`/`ingest.go`'s `handleSamples` tap) without ever blocking ingest (events are dropped under backpressure, counted, never queued unboundedly), and reconciling compiled flows against the database on a ticker plus an explicit change signal so an edit/enable/disable takes effect with no restart -- the same pattern the Modbus poller already uses. The `function`/`expression`/`switch` nodes run in a brand-new embedded, sandboxed JavaScript interpreter (`github.com/dop251/goja`, new pure-Go dependency, isolated in `apps/myiotsan/services/flow_eval.go`) with NO host bindings at all (no filesystem, network, `require`, or `os`) and a hard 100ms-per-call watchdog that interrupts a runaway script -- both guarantees are pinned by tests that try to escape the sandbox and that drive an infinite loop. The safety invariant that makes 'a flow can run arbitrary JavaScript' acceptable: only the dedicated `command` output node can actuate, and it routes through the SAME guarded `CommandService.Issue` chokepoint every manual command, scene, and schedule already uses (actuation-enabled, admin-only, declared bounds, rate limit, full audit, never auto-retried) -- an arbitrary-JS node can shape a *value* but cannot skip a gate, retry a refusal, or reach a device the command layer would otherwise refuse. This is a deliberate, later reversal of `docs/MYIOTSAN_PLAN.md` §8g's original 'no visual node-graph editor' scope line (now documented as §8i, with the reversal called out at §8g and in §9's risk table). P3 added slot-based templates -- a device named by a placeholder (`"$inverter"`) instead of a concrete key makes a flow reusable; `GET /api/flows/{id}/slots` reports what a flow declares and `POST /api/flows/{id}/instantiate` binds every slot to a real device, stamping out a concrete, disabled-by-default copy for an admin to review and enable -- and a shipped builtin 'Solar system' template flow (`apps/myiotsan/services/flow_catalog.go`, seeded idempotently at boot like a device profile) demonstrating the one thing the data-flow model exists to do: combine two telemetry streams (grid + PV power) into a derived self-consumption value via the per-flow JS context, plus a high-grid-import threshold alert. Flow import/export (`.iotflow`, `apps/myiotsan/services/flow_transfer.go`) mirrors the existing `.iotprofile` pattern: an import is never builtin and always arrives disabled. New API (`apps/myiotsan/apis/flows.go`): `GET/POST /api/flows`, `GET/PUT/DELETE /api/flows/{id}`, `POST /api/flows/import`, `GET /api/flows/{id}/export`, `GET /api/flows/{id}/slots`, `POST /api/flows/{id}/instantiate`, `POST /api/flows/{id}/run` (test-fires the flow off the live runtime with a synthetic seed value -- an output node still acts for real, which is the point), and `GET /api/flows/{id}/debug` (the live per-node inspector snapshot). The whole `/api/flows` area is admin-only in the RBAC matrix (`apps/myiotsan/services/rbac.go`) -- unlike scenes/schedules, even READING a flow's graph is denied below admin, because the graph itself can reveal an actuation path. Verified with a dedicated unit suite (`apps/myiotsan/services/flows_test.go`) covering propagation through scale/threshold/deadband, the two JS node types (including the per-flow context surviving across two separate input messages, the mechanism the solar sample depends on), sandbox containment (require/process/filesystem all fail), the watchdog killing a `while(true){}` node within a bounded window, guarded-issuer-only actuation, notification publishing, graph validation rejections, the derived-metric output, and slot detection/substitution/template guards.
compatibility: Backward-compatible for every existing myiotsan install: the new `iot_flow` table is created automatically by the shared entity-reflection bootstrap engine on next boot (no manual migration), starts empty apart from the one seeded builtin 'Solar system' template flow, which is created DISABLED and is a template (its `$inverter` slot is unbound) -- it consumes no readings and fires no outputs until an admin instantiates and enables it. The Flow Engine is entirely additive: it taps the existing decoded-sample stream read-only-in-effect (a flow can only enqueue an event, never block or alter ingest) and only ever actuates through the pre-existing guarded `CommandService.Issue` path, so no existing rule, scene, schedule, or command behavior changes. The whole feature is admin-only server-side, so no existing viewer/operator account gains any new capability. Adds one new Go dependency (`github.com/dop251/goja`, pure-Go, no cgo/system library requirement) -- no new ports, no new config keys, no restart-required settings. The one operator-facing change: a new 'Flows' entry appears under the Automation nav group for admin accounts only.
